functions.axes: X = span, Y = depth, Z = up (as in Rhino). 2D prototypes are drawn in the XZ plane, so a turn inside the drawing is a rotation about Y. 'tip' is the single corner opposite the two supports or loads; 'top', 'base', 'legs', 'ring', 'twigs' name the other parts.

list.name: Divide
list.def: Split a member into n equal segments by adding n − 1 nodes on it.
steps: Pick the member a–b.
Add the nodes p_i = a + (i/n)(b − a) for i = 1 … n − 1.
Replace a–b by the n short members a–p_1, …, p_(n−1)–b.
list.eqNote: Kept: the new nodes are straight-through joints. Putting loads on them is part of the next step.

list.name: Move
list.def: Translate the chosen nodes; the members attached to them follow.
steps: Pick the nodes S.
Move each node p in S to p + v.
Members keep their end nodes, so they stretch and turn.
list.eqNote: Re-check: member directions change, so the forces change, and a C member can turn into T.

list.name: Truncate
list.def: Cut a corner: replace node v by two nodes on its two members and join them with a new member.
steps: Pick the corner v and its two members v–a and v–b.
Mark the points at fraction t from v: v1 = v + t(a − v), v2 = v + t(b − v). With t = 0.5 they are the midpoints of the two sides.
Connect v1–v2 with a new member.
Give the load or support at v to v1 and v2, half each.
Remove v and the short members v–v1, v–v2.
list.eqNote: Re-check: the new member takes the force that turned the corner. It is C where the sides push (arch, V-strut) and T where they pull (cable). The trapezoid is balanced for the two equal loads that replace the single one.

list.name: Branch
list.def: Gather the members of a fan into k groups; each group meets at a new branch node that is joined back to the fan node by one member.
steps: Pick the fan node v and its members.
Split the members into k groups (k = 2: left | right halves; k = 3: symmetric pairs).
For each group add a branch node at fraction t along the group's mean direction from v.
Re-attach the group's members from v to its branch node.
Connect v to each branch node.
list.eqNote: Re-check: each branch node must balance its group. A branch is straight under load when it points along the resultant of its group's loads.

list.name: Extend
list.def: Add a new member from a node along a direction until it reaches a target (the ground or a length L); its far end becomes a support.
steps: Pick the node v and the direction d (for example −Z).
Add the node e where the ray v + s·d meets the target.
Connect v–e.
The support at v moves to e (or e becomes a new support).
list.eqNote: Re-check: the new member carries what the support used to take at v — C for a mast or column, T for a hanger.

list.name: Remove
list.def: Delete the chosen members (or nodes with their members).
steps: Pick the members (or nodes) to delete.
Delete them; a node left with no members is deleted too.
list.eqNote: Re-check: the structure may turn into a mechanism or need new supports. Removing an arch's tie sends its thrust to the supports.

list.name: Connect
list.def: Add a member between two existing nodes, or a closed ring through a list of nodes.
steps: Pick the nodes a and b, or the ring a_1 … a_n.
Add the member a–b (for a ring: a_1–a_2, …, a_n–a_1).
list.eqNote: Re-check: adds a load path. A ring at splayed feet collects their outward push in T; a ring at a waist collects an inward pull in C.

list.name: Scale
list.def: Stretch the whole diagram about an origin, with different factors per axis if needed.
steps: Pick the origin o and the factors (sx, sy, sz).
Move every node p to o + (sx(p − o)_x, sy(p − o)_y, sz(p − o)_z).
list.eqNote: Kept, with C and T unchanged (a parallel projection, Rankine). Force sizes change: in a 2D drawing vertical loads scale by sz/sx.

list.name: Rotate
list.def: Turn the diagram, or the part named first, about an axis by θ.
steps: Pick what turns (default: everything), the axis and the angle θ.
Rotate the nodes about the axis.
Loads turn with the shape by default; write 'gravity' when they stay vertical.
list.eqNote: Kept when the loads turn too (a rigid motion): every force is unchanged. With 'gravity' the loads keep pointing down, so re-check — a bar can switch from C to T.

list.name: Mirror
list.def: Reflect the diagram in a plane.
steps: Pick the plane (vertical YZ, or horizontal XY).
Reflect every node in it.
Loads keep pointing down.
list.eqNote: In a vertical plane: kept, forces unchanged. In a horizontal plane with loads still pointing down, every force changes sign, C↔T: Hooke's hanging chain turns an arch into a cable. Mirror(XY) = FlipLoad ∘ Rotate(Y, 180°) for a symmetric shape, so P1 → P4.

list.name: FlipLoad
list.def: Reverse every load, and so every reaction.
steps: Multiply every load vector by −1.
Supports stay where they are; their reactions reverse too.
list.eqNote: Kept, and every member force changes sign: C becomes T and T becomes C.

list.name: Array
list.def: Make n copies spaced d along a direction; copies that touch share nodes.
steps: Pick the direction (X, Y or Z), the count n and the spacing d (default: the width, so copies just touch).
Copy the diagram n − 1 times, each moved by d.
Merge nodes that coincide.
list.eqNote: Each copy is balanced on its own. Where copies share nodes their forces add; when d is less than the width the copies overlap, so re-check.

list.name: PolarArray
list.def: Make n copies turned by 360°/n about an axis (Z = vertical).
steps: Pick the axis and the count n.
Copy the diagram n − 1 times, each turned a further 360°/n.
Merge nodes on the axis and any that coincide.
list.eqNote: Each copy stays balanced in its own plane. At shared nodes (the axis, the rings) the forces add, so check them; splayed feet need a ring.

list.name: Superpose
list.def: Overlay diagrams in one frame, merge the nodes that coincide and add their loads.
steps: Place each diagram as stated (stack along an axis, cross on an axis, or overlap).
Merge coincident nodes; a member shared by two diagrams carries the sum of their forces.
Add the loads at each merged node.
list.eqNote: If every part is balanced and they meet only at nodes, the sum is balanced (superposition). New contacts or merged members need a re-check.

list.name: Intent
list.def: A step driven by an architectural purpose that no single function captures. Record the type and the goal in words, then the nearest function and its values.
steps: Choose the type: use (people and activity), span (span, clearance, cantilever), light (light and view), site, or construction.
Write the goal in a few words, e.g. Intent(use: room to wait for the bus).
Write ≈ and the nearest function call with its values, e.g. ≈ Move(one side, +X, d=?).
Give the intent its own link, at the step where the decision is made; draw the result and re-check it.
list.eqNote: Always re-check. The nearest function tells you which check applies.

functions.rules: Corner nodes of the 2D prototype are the starting points. A new point is made either between two existing nodes (a fraction t along a member, 0 to 1; t = 0.5 is the midpoint) or beyond a node (along a direction until a stop: ground, a length L, or a member). Whole-diagram moves (Rotate, Scale, Mirror) shift every node together. Name every numeric parameter (n=, t=, θ=, d=, sx=). Write ? for a value still to fill and ≈ for a measured value. Keep one or two functions per link. Every pipeline runs in three stages: geometry (exact rule values) → intent (Intent(type: goal) ≈ Function(values)) → Materialize.
